title: Quagmire IV with two keyword alphabets of 1-9 letters (any letters, no dictionary), plain or read off by columns, repeating key 1-16, solved exactly from both alphabetical tails
k4_result: Decisive cells (expected chance solutions < 1): 1,744 solver cells (key lengths 1-16, Vigenere and Beaufort forms, 4 layouts kw/kw, kw/cols, cols/kw, cols/cols, keyword lengths up to 9 per side) give 0 alphabet pairs. That includes key length 8 with keywords of up to 9+7, 8+8 and 7+9 letters. Extended cells (1 <= expected < 100): 396 cells, 14 pairs (6 at length 13, 8 at length 16), all read; best reading -7.95 per quadgram over 76 quadgrams outside the clues (word coverage 0.33), noise. 16 extended cells at length 8 (keywords 8+9 and 9+9) ran out of their step budget. 236M search steps in all.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s (seeds 18716, 29897, 33883), drawn so that they have no direct clue clash at any key length where K4 has none (8, 11, 12, 13, 16) and have idea 113's loop structure at length 8. Only 3 of 26,899 shuffles qualify; plain shuffles mostly fail at once. Decisive cells: 0, 0 and 1,728 alphabet pairs (the 1,728 all at length 10, Beaufort cols/cols 7+7, best reading -7.41). Extended cells: 48,633, 193 and 788 pairs. Best readings -7.36, -7.97, -7.41. None reaches -5.1. K4 (-7.95, 0 decisive pairs) is inside the controls' range.
planted: 4/4 ranked first of all readings of their text. Random non-word keywords KLQCMJ / AMDLSTXF at key 8 (Vigenere, kw/kw) and AMDLSTXF / KLQCMJ at key 8 (Beaufort, plain side read off by columns). SANBORN / KRIPTOS (misspelled KRYPTOS) at key 11 (Beaufort, kw/kw) and KRIPTOS / SANBORN at key 11 (Vigenere, cipher side by columns). All read back 97/97 at -4.27 to -4.93.
scope_limits: Repeating key only, lengths 1-16 (no sliding or other key rules, nothing over 16). Each alphabet is a keyword of at most 9 different letters followed by the rest in A-Z order, or that alphabet read off by columns of width m. NOT the keyed-column form (columns in the alphabetical order of the keyword), which depends on the keyword's letter order and is not handled by the solver. Keywords over 9 letters and alphabets not built from keywords are not covered. Only cells with fewer than 100 expected chance solutions were run; cells with fewer than 1 expected chance solution are run to the end (exact: 'no pair exists'). At key length 8 the cells with keywords 8+9 and 9+9 letters (expected 1.6 and 28 chance pairs) hit the 1e7-step budget and are not decided. Clue positions taken as exact (no gap slack). Completions of letters in no equation are capped at 30,000 per side per solution, searched by coordinate ascent (no K4 or control solution reached the cap).

negative.family: Quagmire IV, two non-word keyword alphabets
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a Quagmire IV with a repeating key whose plain and cipher alphabets are both keyword alphabets (keywords need not be words: names, misspellings, random letters), possibly read off by columns.
negative.scope: Repeating key 1-16, Vigenere and Beaufort forms, each side a keyword of 1-9 different letters then A-Z order, or that read off by columns of width m (kw/kw, kw/cols, cols/kw, cols/cols); every (key length, m1, m2) cell with < 1 expected chance solution solved exactly (1,744 cells), cells with 1-100 expected solved with a step budget (396 cells, 16 at length 8 over budget); every solution decrypted and read on the big quadgram model.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 alphabet pairs in all 1,744 decisive cells; 14 chance pairs in extended cells, best reading -7.95 (controls: 3 K4-like shuffles, decisive 0/0/1,728 pairs, best readings -7.36/-7.97/-7.41; planted 4/4 ranked first, read back 97/97 at -4.27 to -4.93). Not covered: keyed-column alphabets, keywords over 9 letters, key 8 with keywords 8+9 or 9+9, other key rules.

follow_ups: Key length 8 with keywords of 8+9 and 9+9 letters: the solver needs about 1e8-1e9 steps per cell (minutes to an hour in Python); expected chance pairs are only 1.6 and 28, so every solution could still be read. About 16 cells per text.

The keyed-column form (columns read in the alphabetical order of the keyword): with the column order fixed, every letter carries a count of keyword letters below it, so the same tail bookkeeping applies with one count per letter; enumerating the m! column orders is cheap for m <= 6 at key lengths other than 8.
Sliding keys (running sum of a repeating word) with two keyword alphabets: idea 86's slide equations carry over unchanged to the two-sided solver.
